sections.title: Publishing
sections.heading: Build a static site
sections.text: Run this from the directory containing docs/. npx grimoire3d build The output is dist/ by default. To choose a different output directory, use --out-dir site or set outDir: site in grimoire.yml. The CLI protects existing files in an unrelated output directory.

sections.title: Publishing
sections.heading: Upload the output
sections.text: Publish the contents of the output directory with a static host such as Cloudflare Pages or GitHub Pages. This documentation uses GitHub Pages. Upload the complete output so chapter URLs, styles, images, and video work together. Chapter URLs have their own HTML files, so direct links work on a host that serves directory indexes. For a site under a subpath, such as a GitHub Pages project at https://example.github.io/handbook/, include that path in siteUrl before you build. Configure your site metadata before you publish.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.text: Place grimoire.yml in the project directory where you run Grimoire3D. title: Engineering Handbook docsDir: handbook description: Setup, operations, and release notes for the project. siteUrl: https://docs.example.com/ author: Documentation Team socialImage: assets/share.avif locale: en magicMode: true footer: label: Engineering Team url: https://example.com/engineering/ Both serve and build read docs/ directly under the working directory by default. Set docsDir to use a different path, or pass --docs-dir to override it for one run. Relative paths are resolved from the working directory.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Library footer
sections.text: Set footer.label to show a publisher, team, or project name at the end of the bookshelf and index. Set footer.url to link that name to an absolute HTTP(S) address. Omit the URL for a plain label. The footer also links to the Grimoire3D repository.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Titles and social cards
sections.text: The build produces standalone HTML for every chapter, including the text, navigation, page title, description, and Open Graph metadata. Visitors and crawlers can read the articles without JavaScript. The site title defaults to the name in package.json or the project directory name. Use title to choose a different site title. Set siteUrl to get canonical URLs and a sitemap. Set socialImage to an absolute HTTP(S) URL or an image path relative to the chosen Markdown folder. At the domain root the build also emits robots.txt pointing to the sitemap.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Google Tag Manager and additional head tags
sections.text: To include the same tags on the library and each book and chapter page, add this setting to grimoire.yml. headFile: head.html Create head.html next to grimoire.yml. <!-- Paste the head snippet from your Google Tag Manager installation dialog here. --> <!-- To verify site ownership, replace your-token and uncomment the next line. --> <!-- <meta name="google-site-verification" content="your-token"> --> Follow Google's web container setup to get the snippet for your site. The file contains individual script, meta, link, or style tags. Scripts in it run on the published site with the same privileges as the rest of the page, so use snippets from sources you trust. Run npx grimoire3d build to insert the fragment. To test the tags before publishing, serve the built output and open a library or chapter URL. The live serve preview skips the fragment so ordinary editing does not send analytics traffic. The build reports and rejects tags Grimoire3D manages, such as <title>, the canonical link, and its description and Open Graph fields. Use the site and chapter settings for those values. Without a headFile setting, the site uses its built-in head.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Chapter metadata
sections.text: Supply title, description, or socialImage in a chapter's YAML front matter. A chapter-level image path is relative to that chapter. --- title: Deployment guide description: Publish the project to a static web host. socialImage: ./assets/deploy.avif --- # Deployment

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Keep a chapter out of search results
sections.text: Set noindex: true in the chapter's front matter. --- noindex: true --- # Review notes The generated chapter remains readable by URL, and its HTML tells search engines to leave the page out of search results. Its URL is also left out of the sitemap. If this is the book's first chapter, URLs that open directly to that chapter get the same directive. A site with only opted-out URLs skips sitemap generation. Share the URL for a chapter or a specific heading, for example /read/publishing/metadata/#chapter-metadata. Existing links that start with #/ also work.

sections.title: Site settings and SEO
sections.heading: Book index example
sections.text: In docs/handbook/index.md, combine the title, summary, share image, and reading order in YAML front matter. --- title: Engineering Handbook description: Setup, examples, and publishing steps for project developers. socialImage: ./assets/share.webp noindex: false cover: teal coverImage: ./assets/cover.webp category: Engineering date: "2026-11-20" chapters: - setup.md - examples/ - reference.md --- Add the actual image files and use paths relative to this index.md. title names the book and its opening chapter; description and socialImage describe that chapter for search and sharing. Other chapters can supply their own summaries and images. Use cover, coverImage, category, and date in the book's index.md. Use chapters in any folder's index.md to order its direct children. Put the site URL, language, and author in grimoire.yml. siteUrl supplies the base for canonical URLs and the sitemap. For public chapters, omit noindex or set it to false, and choose a summary and share image that match the content.
